sections.content: The acceptance skill coordinates deterministic evidence for one explicit execution plan. It requires frozen baselines, complete manifests, contracts, registries, typed requests, hash-bound candidate and knowledge context, validated inputs, and fail-closed prerequisite checks. It does not change code or perform release actions.
sections.title: Acceptance skill

sections.content: The VDD execution plan separates lifecycle ownership, requires complete-directory requests for VDD work, hash-bound scope and knowledge preflight, bounded repairs, immutable history, acceptance evidence, and terminal validation. The completion report records implementation-complete status after policy, projection, migration, replay, package, CLI, schema, and diff checks. The validator requires five files and six registered Python commands to pass.
sections.title: Execution plan and validation

sections.content: The command registry defines shell-free repository-root validators, replay probes, package and workflow checks, and bounded timeouts, without execution outcomes. The implementation contract covers RMAP slices, historical replay, negative and positive probes, stable-candidate evaluation, downstream replay, receipts, repair closures, lifecycle distinctions, and forbidden unrelated changes.
